extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, securities lawyers, auditors, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for SEC-required climate-related disclosures (subpart 1500) and related financial statement effects (Article 14), including what counts as forward-looking statements, safe-harbor scope, and required financial note disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSLRA safe harbor applies to transition plans, scenario analysis, internal carbon pricing, and targets/goals disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Because transition planning, scenario analysis, and internal carbon pricing involve assumptions, judgments, and predictions about future events, such disclosures constitute 'forward-looking statements' for purposes of the PSLRA safe harbors, and the Commission is providing a safe harbor for these disclosures to avoid having to disentangle forward-looking from factual information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The safe harbor treats all information required by subpart 1500 concerning transition plans, scenario analysis, internal carbon pricing, and targets and goals as forward-looking statements (except historical facts). The extension is intended to encourage more comprehensive disclosures and reduce compliance burdens that would arise from having to separate factual from forward-looking content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory definition — types of forward-looking statements covered
rubrics_metrics.description: The PSLRA statutory provisions define 'forward-looking statement' to include, among other types: (1) projections of revenues, income, earnings, capital expenditures, capital structure, or other financial items; (2) statements of management's plans and objectives for future operations; (3) statements of future economic performance, including MD&A-type discussions; (4) statements of the assumptions underlying the above; and (5) statements containing a projection or estimate specified by Commission rule or regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a registrant's subpart 1500 disclosures contain one or more of these statements, they will fall within the PSLRA statutory definition and may rely on the PSLRA safe harbors provided the other PSLRA requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSLRA safe harbor availability remains subject to PSLRA requirements (meaningful cautionary statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with the PSLRA, the safe harbor protections apply only if the forward-looking statement is accompanied by a meaningful cautionary statement that identifies important factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those in the forward-looking statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must include cautionary language identifying material risk factors and uncertainties as required by PSLRA case law and statute for the safe harbor protection to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical facts are excluded from the safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules' forward-looking safe harbor will not be available for statements consisting solely of historical fact because such information does not involve assumptions, judgments, and predictions about future events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-exclusive examples of historical facts excluded from the safe harbor include information related to carbon offsets or RECs described pursuant to a target or goal (e.g., the amount of carbon avoidance represented by an offset, the nature/source of the offset/REC) and a registrant's statements about material expenditures actually incurred. Statements in consolidated GAAP financial statements are also excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor extension to entities/transactions otherwise excluded from PSLRA
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules extend the Item 1507 safe harbor to forward-looking statements made in connection with offerings or issuers otherwise excluded by PSLRA (e.g., blank check company offerings, penny stock issuers, rollup transactions, IPOs, partnerships, LLCs, direct participation investment programs) for the specified subpart 1500 disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission determined extension is consistent with the public interest because such entities may face material climate-related risks requiring subpart 1500 disclosures; the extension should encourage comprehensive disclosures and mitigate perceived compliance costs affecting capital formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSLRA safe harbor does not cover forward-looking statements included in GAAP financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The PSLRA safe harbor does not apply to forward-looking statements included in financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. Consequently, forward-looking statements included in consolidated financial statements or incorporated by reference from the financial statements into subpart 1500 disclosures are not eligible for the Item 1507 safe harbor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants cannot rely on Item 1507 for any forward-looking content that is part of audited GAAP financial statements; such content remains outside the statutory safe harbor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scopes 1 and 2 emissions disclosures not included in safe harbor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission declines to include Scopes 1 and 2 emissions disclosures within the scope of the Item 1507 safe harbor because the methodologies underlying the calculation of those scopes are fairly well-established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these methodologies are established, the Commission concluded a private litigation safe harbor is unnecessary for Scopes 1 and 2 disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 14 financial disclosure applicability trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant is required to file the disclosure required by subpart 1500 in a filing that also requires audited financial statements, then the registrant must disclose in a note to its financial statements certain disaggregated financial-statement metrics (Article 14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the avoidance of doubt, a registrant is required to comply with Article 14 even if it does not have information to disclose pursuant to subpart 1500, as long as the Commission filing requires the registrant to comply with subpart 1500.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of financial-statement metrics (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rules would have required disclosure falling under three categories: Financial Impact Metrics; Expenditure Metrics; and Financial Estimates and Assumptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal's Financial Impact Metrics would have required disaggregation of impacts from severe weather, other natural conditions, and transition activities across financial statement line items; however the final rules decline to adopt the broad Financial Impact Metrics and instead narrow scope (see other entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rule focus: disclose capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses from severe weather and other natural conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules require disclosure of capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, and losses incurred as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions, and require registrants to disclose where on the balance sheet and income statement these amounts are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These amounts are quantitative and derived from transactions and amounts recorded in the registrant's books and records. The final rules narrowed the scope compared to the proposal to reduce burdens on registrants. The rules do not require disclosure of statement of cash flows impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-percent disclosure threshold retained in narrowed form (aggregate categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules retain a one-percent disclosure threshold but registrants will not apply it on a line-item basis; instead the one-percent threshold applies only to two categories of aggregate amounts: (1) expenditures expensed as incurred and losses; and (2) capitalized costs and charges, each incurred as a result of severe weather events and other natural conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules use different denominators for the disclosure thresholds compared to the proposal and include de minimis thresholds to address commenter burden concerns. The narrower application (aggregate categories rather than line items) is intended to mitigate compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of costs related to carbon offsets and RECs (material-component test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to disclose capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, and losses related to carbon offsets and RECs is not subject to the one-percent threshold; disclosure is required if carbon offsets and RECs have been used as a material component of a registrant's plans to achieve its disclosed climate-related targets or goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties covered should know with reasonable certainty information about purchased offsets or RECs (amounts, nature, source); such historical factual elements are not eligible for the Item 1507 safe harbor, but the financial-statement effects are required to be disclosed in Article 14 when material under the tests above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material expenditures related to mitigation/transition/targets to be disclosed outside financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of requiring disclosure of expenditures related to transition activities in the financial statements, the final rules require registrants to disclose material expenditures related to (1) activities to mitigate or adapt to climate-related risk (in management's assessment), (2) disclosed transition plans, and (3) disclosed targets and goals outside of the financial statements as part of Regulation S-K amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These disclosures are required outside of the audited financial statements (e.g., in narrative sections) and are separate from Article 14 note requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial-statement note disclosures subject to audit and ICFR
rubrics_metrics.description: Including the climate-related financial statement disclosures in a note to the financial statements will subject these disclosures to independent audit and registrants' internal control over financial reporting (ICFR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjecting the disclosures to audit and ICFR is expected to improve consistency, quality, and reliability of the information, benefiting investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rules apply across sectors and to smaller reporting companies (SRCs) and emerging growth companies (EGCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules apply to public companies generally (not limited to certain sectors) and will apply to SRCs and EGCs, although the rules include narrower scope, de minimis thresholds, and longer phased compliance periods for SRCs and EGCs to mitigate burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission declined to exempt SRCs/EGCs because severe weather events and natural conditions can pose significant risks to companies of all sizes; accommodations (de minimis thresholds and phased compliance) are included to lessen burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for certain business-combination private companies
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rules, including amendments to Regulation S-X, will not apply to a private company that is a party to a business combination transaction, as defined by Securities Act Rule 165(f), involving a securities offering registered on Form S-4 or F-4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This carve-out is discussed in section II.L.3 of the release and limits the application of the final rules in that specific transaction context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Financial Impact Metrics (examples and aggregation approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal (not adopted as originally written) would have required disclosure of financial impacts from severe weather and transition activities on any relevant consolidated financial statement line item if aggregated impact met a one-percent threshold; impacts would have been reported aggregated line-by-line for negative and positive impacts separately, with aggregation of absolute values used to determine threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of impacts that may have been required: changes to revenues/costs from business disruptions or supply chains; impairment charges and changes to carrying amounts of assets; changes to loss contingencies or reserves; changes to total expected insured losses. For transition activities, examples included revenue or cost changes from emissions pricing, cash flow changes from upstream cost changes, asset carrying amount changes due to reduced useful life, and interest expense changes tied to climate-linked financial instruments. The Commission provided these examples to aid comparability and issuer implementation, though the broad line-item approach was not adopted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for narrower scope: avoid burdens of line-item tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Many commenters indicated companies do not currently track climate-related impacts by financial statement line item and lack systems/processes to do so; the Commission narrowed final rules to mitigate costs and burdens while providing decision-useful information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rules aim to balance investor needs for disaggregated financial information about climate impacts with registrant burdens by focusing on discrete, auditable categories (capitalized costs, expenditures expensed, charges, losses) and limiting the threshold application.
